newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia may restrict small banks' expansion-Anwar.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia may restrict small banks' expansion-Anwar.

text.p: Malaysia is planning to restrict branch expansion by banks which have not attained Tier-I status under the country's two-tier banking system, Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Friday.

"Banking institutions which fail to make the mark on the requirement on shareholders' funds for Tier-I status may also no longer be allowed to open new branches freely," Anwar said at a fund managers' conference.
Anwar did not give any further details.
Malaysia's central bank, Bank Negara has been urging Malaysian financial institutions to merge and grow in size as the country opens up the banking industry to more competition.
The central bank has instituted a two-tier banking system, under which larger, better-managed banks come under Tier-I and are allowed to operate in a liberal regulatory environment.
Tier-I banks are expected to increase their shareholders' funds to one billion ringgit by the year 2000.
"Today financial institutions which meet the level of shareholders' funds required for Tier-I status are allowed to be participants in the interbank market," Anwar said.
